newsitem.title: USA: CyberOptics sees possible market turn.
newsitem.headline: CyberOptics sees possible market turn.

text.p: CyberOptics Corp said fourth quarter sales could indicate the surface mount technology market, weak through 1996 due to global over-capacity, is entering a new round of capacity expansion.
"However...any such rebound may not become fully evident until later in the coming year," the company said.
CyberOptics' 1996 performance was hurt by "sharply reduced sales of Laser Align sensors to original equipment manufacturers of large-capacity pick-and-place assembly equipment," the company said.

"This weakness was partially offset by increased demand for LaserAlign among OEMs of mid-range surface mount technology equipment as well as by increased sales of solder paste inspection systems," the company said.
The company said it believes "1997 is currently shaping up as a year of improved sales and earnings."

CyberOptics Tuesday reported net income of $416,000 on revenues of $6.7 million for the fourth quarter of 1996, compared to net income of $1.9 million on revenues of $10.5 million in year-ago quarter, which was the strongest three-month period in the company's history.
For 1996, net income came to $2.2 million, compared to $4.8 million in 1995. Revenues totaled $28.1 million in 1996, compared to $30.5 million last year.
CyberOptics makes non-contact process management systems using laser and vision technologies and software.
